why: The statement asks one yes/no question. An infinite finitely presented periodic group answers it in full, in the 'no' direction, so both OpenAI rows are scope whole. The group contradicts 'every such group is finite', which makes it a counterexample and the direction refuted. Nobody has reviewed either row: Lean on its own is not digestion (F7), and no person has engaged with the claim. Both rows are doubtful rather than credible because the release carries its own warnings and withdrew sibling manuscripts, but no error specific to this construction has been found, so nothing knocks them down. AI role is generated: the repository says the manuscripts and proof artifacts were produced by the internal model. That attribution is repository-level, not specific to this family, and I accepted it. The pre-2024 papers give: Ivanov's weakly finitely presented groups and Burnside embeddings, the Olshanskii–Sapir torsion-by-cyclic group, and Wagner's torsion subgroup are all variants. Sapir's note is a survey (none). Button–Thillaisundaram and Thillaisundaram settle the restricted class of presentations with positive p-deficiency: such groups are not periodic, which confirms the statement for that class, so they are cases.
doubts: The two OpenAI rows overlap: openai-2026-f-p-periodic and openai-math-247 describe the same construction, St₁₂(R), from the same release. The second row also bundles the residually finite 2-group companion (dated 5 October 2026). I kept both rows as the record splits them. They agree on every answer except the date (23 September vs 6 October 2026). Whether the AI credit for this particular family is accurate depends on repository-level wording only. Thillaisundaram 2011 depends on a snippet saying the surjection target is Z. Ivanov 2002 counts as digested only because it appeared in an AMS Contemp. Math. volume; its refereeing was not confirmed. That row is discarded as a variant either way.
